title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 6th District
area: St. Cloud and the northern/western Twin Cities exurbs, including Otsego, Elk River and Anoka County.

context.text: Incumbent Tom Emmer (R), the House Majority Whip, advanced from the August 11, 2026 Republican primary. Doug Chapin won the Democratic primary unopposed among ballot-qualified candidates.

candidates.name: Tom Emmer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 80.9% of the vote against Michael Foley and Chris Corey.

summary.text: Emmer is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 6th District, first elected in 2014, and serves as House Majority Whip. He sits on the Committee on Financial Services, where he is Vice Chair.

background.text: Born in South Bend, Indiana; graduated from St. Thomas Academy in Mendota Heights, Minnesota.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Alaska in 1984 and a law degree from William Mitchell College of Law in 1988; practiced as a trial attorney and founded his own law firm.
Served on the Independence City Council (1995-2002) and the Delano City Council (2003-2004) before serving in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2005 to 2011.

priorities.text: Serves as House Majority Whip, responsible for coordinating House Republican votes on legislation.
Focuses on financial services and digital-asset policy as Vice Chair of the Committee on Financial Services.
Lists agriculture, law enforcement, mental health, and transportation as district priorities on his official website.

positions.summary: Says law enforcement has worked under repeated budget cuts and that Congress should stand behind officers, and highlights his work supporting law-enforcement programs.
positions.quote: Our law enforcement officers sacrifice so much to keep our communities safe, the very least we can do is stand behind them.

record.text: Elected House Majority Whip for the 118th Congress and continues in that role in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Serves as Vice Chair of the Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Previously served on the Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology and Inclusion (2023-2024) and the Subcommittee on Investor Protection, Entrepreneurship and Capital Markets (2021-2022).

candidates.researchNotes: Emmer's official issues pages (agriculture, blockchain, crypto caucus, law enforcement, mental health, transportation) rarely address the guide's 15 issue statements directly; most map to topics outside those categories (agriculture, digital-asset policy) rather than a documented stance on them, so only one position could be added without inferring from party or general rhetoric.

candidates.name: Doug Chapin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary.

summary.text: Chapin is a longtime election-policy expert and attorney running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent Tom Emmer, campaigning on the economy, healthcare, and government functioning.

background.text: Worked for a decade at the University of Minnesota's Humphrey School of Public Affairs, where he founded the nation's first online certificate program in Election Administration.
Spent over a decade leading The Pew Charitable Trusts' elections team and founded electionline.org in 2001, a nonpartisan source for election policy news.

Holds a J.D. from Georgetown University Law Center, a Master's in Public Administration from Harvard's Kennedy School, and a bachelor's degree from Princeton University; has practiced election and ethics law and served as elections counsel to Democrats on the U.S. Senate Rules Committee.

priorities.text: Build an economy that works for everyone.
priorities.quote: Build an economy that works for everyone

priorities.text: Build healthcare that works for everyone.
priorities.quote: Build healthcare that works for everyone

priorities.text: Build a government that works, drawing on his background in election administration.

candidates.researchNotes: Chapin completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey but stated only general campaign themes; no campaign website or additional issue-specific statements were found.
